The petitioner-appellants are before this Court calling in question the judgment and award dated 26th November, 2016 passed in MVC No.590 of 2015 by the Additional Motor Vehicle NC:
2023:KHC-D:9151-DB Accident Claims Tribunal at Honnavar, wherein the Tribunal dismissed the claim petition.
2.

Additional Motor Vehicle NC:
2023:KHC-D:9151-DB Accident Claims Tribunal at Honnavar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: For the sake of convenience, the parties in this appeal are referred to their status and rank before the Tribunal.
3. The petitioners in this case serve as the legal representatives of the late Mohammed Gouse, whose life was tragically died in a motorcycle accident.

On that fateful morning of May 24, 2015, at 5:10 am, Mohammed Gouse was a passenger on a motorcycle bearing the Registration No. KA- 47/K-9723, navigating the bustling National Highway 66 from Bhatkal to Kundapura.

However,
their journey took a dire turn as the motorcycle's rider recklessly sped down the highway, eventually colliding with an unknown vehicle near Navunda Masjid in the peaceful village of Maravanthe.
The Mohammed Gouse was grievously injured that necessitated an urgent transfer to Adarsha Hospital in Udupi.
Despite the valiant efforts of medical professionals, his injuries proved fatal, leading to his untimely demise.
On this ground, the petitioners preferred the claim petition seeking compensation.
4. Upon being served with the notice, respondent No.1 has come forward and submitted a written statement in which NC: 2023:KHC-D:9151-DB they dispute the claims made in the petition.
Respondent No.1 asserts that the motorcycle's rider, Mr. Irfan R. Bangalkote, cannot be held responsible for the accident that transpired.

According to their account, it was an unforeseeable event when, at Navund Masjid, an unidentified vehicle collided with their motorcycle, resulting in the injuries sustained by Mohammed Gouse, who was riding as a pillion passenger.
They firmly contend that the accident was primarily due to the negligence of the unknown vehicle's driver.
It is important to note that the motorcycle belonging to respondent No.1 was insured by respondent No.2-Insurance Company, and the rider possessed a valid and effective driving license.
Consequently, respondent No.1 argues that if any compensation is deemed necessary, it is the responsibility of respondent No.2-Insurance Company to provide the requisite compensation.
The respondent No.2 appeared and filed the written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition as false and sought for dismissal of the petition.

5. Based on the pleadings the Tribunal has framed the following issues:
NC: 2023:KHC-D:9151-DB (1) Whether the petitioners prove that deceased Mohammed Gouse being pillion rider of motorcycle bearing No.KA-47/K-9723 met with the accident on 24.05.2015 at about 5.10 am near Navunda Masjid, Maravanthe village, Kundapur Taluk and succumbed to injuries in the accident, due to rash and negligent riding of the said motor cycle by its rider as alleged in the petition?
(2) Whether the respondent No.2 proves that the rider for the vehicle bearing No.KA-47/K-9723 was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident?
(3) Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount?
(4) What order or award?

3 6.
In order to support their case, petitioner No.1 got examined as PW1 and got marked six documents as Exhibits P1 to P6.
Respondents did not chose to examine anyone, however got marked two documents as Exhibits R1 and R2.
After hearing the arguments on both sides, the Tribunal answered issues in the negative and dismissed the claim petition with costs.
Being aggrieved by the dismissal of the claim petition, the appellant-claimants are before this Court in this appeal.
In view of the above finding, the Tribunal dismissed the petition with costs.
Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award, the appellant-claimants have preferred this appeal.
SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF APPELLANTS 8.
The learned counsel representing the appellant- claimants has put forth several crucial arguments in this case.
Firstly, it is contended that the Tribunal erred in not duly considering the evidence and documents that were presented during the proceedings.
The appellant-claimants originally filed their application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, seeking compensation.
However, they now wish to amend their claim petition to fall under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
This proposed amendment also includes a limitation on their claim, restricting it to the deceased's income of Rs.40,000 per annum.
It is important to note that this amendment request was inadvertently omitted during the initial NC: 2023:KHC-D:9151-DB proceedings.

Therefore, the learned counsel is advocating for the matter to be remanded to the Tribunal, allowing the appellant-claimants the opportunity to file the necessary application for this amendment under Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.
This is to ensure that the claim aligns with the appropriate legal provisions and accurately represents the circumstances of the case.
Accordingly, on all these grounds sought to remand the matter to the Tribunal with a direction to permit the appellant-claimants to file necessary application before the Tribunal.
SUBMISSIONS ON BEHALF OF INSURER 9.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company submitted his arguments that the Tribunal has appreciated the evidence on record in accordance with law.
The appellants have not made out any ground to interfere with the impugned Judgment and Award and on all these grounds sought for dismissal of the appeal.
10. We have carefully examined the materials placed before this Court.

11. Based on the complaint lodged by Mohammed Irfan, the Gangolli Police initiated a case,
registered as Crime NC: 2023:KHC-D:9151-DB No.77 of 2015, against the unidentified vehicle for alleged offenses under Sections 279, 338, and 304A of the Indian Penal Code, as well as Section 134(a) and (b) of the Motor Vehicles Act.
Subsequently, they filed a First Information Report with the Court.
Following this, the police conducted an spot mahazar, including the preparation of a rough sketch and the inquest panchnama of the deceased, all done in the presence of witnesses.

Smt. Dilshad Kaladgi, W/O. Late ... vs Mohamed, Basha, S/O. Abdul Rehman on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87864482/
4 12.
Upon thorough investigation, the Investigation Officer filed a charge sheet against respondent No.1, the rider of the motorcycle.

However, it is evident from the materials presented to this Court that the appellant-claimants have not submitted a copy of the charge sheet issued by the Investigating Officer, which is crucial for a comprehensive assessment of the case.

The learned counsel representing the appellants has informed this Court of their intention to file a necessary application to amend the provision of law, specifically changing it from Section 166 to Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

Additionally, they plan to amend the presumed income of the deceased to an amount of Rs. 40,000 per NC: 2023:KHC-D:9151-DB annum, in line with the compensation criteria outlined in Schedule II of Section 163A of the Motor Vehicles Act.

13. Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the appellant-claimants, so also,
the facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the considered opinion that it is just and proper to remand the matter to the Tribunal permitting the appellant-claimants to take necessary steps for amendment of provision of law and also the income of the deceased, as sought for.
